<reason>PRO won the burden-default clash. CON's irreversibility plus test-incompleteness case was strong, but PRO showed pre-release adversarial thresholds with safety margins handle it, gave a concrete withholding trigger when pressed, and exposed that CON's affirmative-approval still relies on the same incomplete testing. Permanence vs magnitude gave the cleaner vote rule.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's Rebuttal 2 through Closing dilemma that reversing the burden does not cure uncertainty: if finite conservative evidence can justify release it is a threshold, if every future adaptation must be excluded it is an indefinite ban.</best_rebuttal>
